what: The customer drawer looked squashed in the F09 1440 screenshot: labels cut to 'Pr...' and 'My...' and a tiny logo.
why: The screenshot helper resized the window and captured while the generated drawer was still animating its width, so the picture showed a mid-animation frame.
workaround: Helper waits until the logo reaches full width (settleLayout) before capturing at 1440; new drawer test checks labels and logo width.

what: The generated layout stores the mini drawer state in browser storage (webshop-config) and recomputes it only when the window crosses a size tier, so a browser that was once small opens collapsed on a desktop screen, also after reload.
why: Behaviour not described in the catalog; the builder searched the kb twice and found nothing on drawer state.
workaround: Render-nothing DrawerExpander registered as the documented AppBar extra component opens the drawer at lg and xl widths on load and on size change, in both actors.
proposed_target: generated layout drawer (miniDrawer persistence); document the workaround in ui-hooks.md

what: The customer API returned stock, active and variants on the product list and details (data leak), because the customer used the admin-facing product transfer object.
why: Own design mistake from earlier rounds: the customer product access pointed at the mapped ProductInfo, which carries admin-only fields.
workaround: New mapped transfer object ShopProductInfo without stock, active and variants; Customer.products points at it; ProductInfo stays admin only; test watches server answers for a browsing customer.

what: Renaming the customer product transfer object forced hand edits of custom frontend files (renamed custom-implementation file, new constants, container and type paths) and deletion of stale generated customer folders.
why: Custom frontend file names and constants are derived from the transfer object name; stale generated containers stay behind after a model change. The builder found the recovery steps in build-process.md.
workaround: git mv of the custom file, search-and-replace of names and paths, removal of generated pages, dialogs, containers and services folders, then regenerate.
proposed_target: catalog/agent-docs/deployment/build-process.md (renaming a transfer object: which generated and custom files follow)

what: Admin product table columns needed fixed widths at 1440 px, but the builder did not know the unit or value format of DataColumn.width and set plain integers (170, 120, 100 and so on).
why: The CLI schema shows width as a plain string; the catalog says fixed pixel width but the builder did not find a value example for the attribute.
workaround: Plain integer widths set on every column; all columns and row actions fit at 1440 and the admin tests now run at 1440.

what: The numeric price column cannot be shown formatted or sorted another documented way, so the admin table shows 79.9 and the builder only renamed the header to 'Price (EUR)' to fit it.
why: The DataColumn schema has formatValue and sort settings, but the builder found no documented way to format a numeric column value (R1-1 and R6-4 remain open).
workaround: Kept the numeric column with a shorter label and a width; formatting left open.

what: The CLI query for DataColumn and DataFilter returned nothing until 'fill' had been run on the transfer object, so the builder first thought the table columns did not exist.
why: Column and filter elements are created by fill, not by create; the query output gives no hint of that.
workaround: Ran fill on the transfer object, then queried again.
proposed_target: judo-cli query output or judo-cli.md note on fill

what: Creating a transfer object with a mapping auto-creates the mapped members (lineTotal, total and so on), so hand-made derived members with the same names gave 'not unique' and binding errors on validation.
why: Behaviour of mapped transfer objects not described where the builder looked; the same lesson was learned in R7 (R7-14) and repeated.
workaround: Deleted the duplicated hand-made members and kept the auto-created ones; validation passed.
proposed_target: catalog/best-practices/model/unmapped-transfer-dto.md or a mapped-transfer-object page: mapping creates members

what: Validator warnings appeared after the Customer product access changed: 'Columns are not defined for the viewable table' and 'Principal of actor Customer should not have relations and operations'.
why: Not explained by the builder; the warnings were noted in the CLI output and not acted on.

what: Running pnpm format by hand failed because the lockfile entries were newer than the minimumReleaseAge policy.
why: pnpm policy in the generated frontend rejects lockfile entries published within the cutoff; the real build failure was the duplicate import (c04-13), so this was a side issue in the investigation.
proposed_target: generated frontend pnpm configuration (minimumReleaseAge vs lockfile)

what: An OperationForm placed directly in a view fails UI validation (ActionContainerSameWithActionDefinition, NamedElementHaveToBeInApplication); the operation must sit in an ActionGroup, and the catalog says direct placement works.
why: The catalog section on operation wiring says OperationForm inside View or Form works; the transformation rejects it. The openspec sweep already lists ActionGroup-wrapped OperationForms as an open item (FR-033). Even inside an ActionGroup, the validator still reported action container errors after the wrap (session:L2494).
workaround: Moved both operations into an ActionGroup named actions, set label Actions and featuredActions=1; for checkout the action container errors cleared only after it became void with generateActionsHook=true (validation passed, session:L2522).
proposed_target: catalog/agent-docs/model/ui-authoring-guide.md section 10 (OperationForm in ActionGroup is required; constraints on action container)

what: postCallAccessNavigation cannot be cleared once set, and move --index had no effect on the position of the action group; move --after did reorder the menu entries.
why: CLI behaviour: unset is refused for this attribute and move with an index is ignored for these elements.
workaround: Left postCallAccessNavigation set (the clear attempt was refused, session:L2481); used move --after for menu order, since move --index had no effect.
proposed_target: judo-cli update and move (unset of postCallAccessNavigation, move --index)

what: An operation with an output and an input dialog makes the generated dialog file import the output type twice (import type { OrderInfo, OrderInfo, ... }); Biome rejects it as a parse error and the frontend build stops.
why: Generator bug. Tried mapped output, output with a relation to the same type, and output with one primitive: all failed the same way. The catalog's operation-return-type-navigation pattern (return the destination type from the operation output) is therefore blocked.
workaround: Made checkout a void operation; the new order is opened through the generated dialog actions hook (see c04-14).
proposed_target: generator: dialog types for operations whose output is also a post-call navigation target

what: Checkout is a void operation. The new order opens through the generated dialog actions hook (postCheckoutForCartInfoAction, generateActionsHook=true), which lists the newest order and navigates to it.
why: Only route left after the duplicate-import generator bug (c04-13); it costs one extra list call and deviates from FUNCTIONS F21 (operation returns the created order).
workaround: Java checkout is void; the hook navigates to the newest order.

what: A business fault shows in the generated fault dialog as the error code letter by letter (0: N, 1: O, 2: T ...), not as a readable message.
why: The generated 422 handler opens the dialog from the first key of the response body; the body starts with 'code', not the fault. The catalog describes the body with the fault key first, which is wrong for this version.
workaround: Error handler interceptor shows the fault's message as a snackbar (documented route in the frontend error-handling page).
proposed_target: generated error-handling.ts (422 handler takes first key); catalog body order in error-handling.md

what: Stock overflow is a modeled fault (ShopFault with message) declared on addToCart; the UI reads the message through a custom error interceptor and shows it as a snackbar.
why: Modeled faults are the documented business-error route (error-handling-guide); the generated dialog cannot show the message (c04-15).

what: After generate or build, target/judo-cli.jar disappeared, so every CLI call failed with 'Unable to access jarfile' until generate-root was run again.
why: generate and build do not recreate the CLI jar; only generate-root (or the validate goal) copies it. Known from earlier rounds (R7-7, S01).
workaround: Helper script .scratch/ensure-cli.sh runs generate-root when the jar is missing; used before every CLI step.
proposed_target: catalog/agent-docs/model/judo-cli.md (generate and build do not restore the jar)

what: The builder did not consult the kb before source searches: about 20 kb guard warnings ('repeated source searching, still no kb consult'); the orchestrator later counted kb 6 of 161 calls.
why: Builder habit: catalog and generated code were read with ctx_execute and grep instead of kb_search and kb_get first.

what: The builder said the kb had no entry for the generated DAO method names, error handler and customization constants; the DAO names were read from the generated SDK instead.
why: Claim is unverified: data-access-guide.md exists in the catalog and the builder read it at session:L2364 for another question. The kb-first search was not run for these names.
workaround: Read generated SDK and frontend source directly.

what: A reload added to the screenshot helper (to lay out the drawer) closed open dialogs, so six admin tests failed until the reload was removed.
why: Own test-helper mistake made while fixing R8-1.
workaround: Removed the reload calls from the helpers; admin suite then passed 30 of 30.

what: Card locators matched other products whose descriptions mention the product name ('Hiking socks' matched two cards), giving strict-mode violations in the F20 tests.
why: Locator by text, not by the exact card name.
workaround: card() helper filters by the exact card-name element.

what: The F19 and F20 tests waited for dialog buttons with names Add to cart, Ok, Check out, and then Submit; the wrong button names and the dialog expectation cost several test runs.
why: Test expectations written before the generated dialog labels were known.
workaround: Button regex changed to Ok or Submit; the readable error is checked as a snackbar text.

what: The admin and shop product counts read 9 instead of 8 in the S04 and S08 tests after the F01 category test failed, probably leaving an extra product behind.
why: Inferred from the sequence of failed runs (level1 F01 failed at session:L2577); not confirmed by the builder.

what: Menu order is not taken from the model: the drawer shows Products, My orders, My addresses, Cart, My profile although the model lists Cart second; move commands had no effect on the generated order.
why: Menu order is decided by the generated drawer; the builder did not use the menu customizer hook.

what: No catalog text found by the builder on whether a custom operation rolls back on error; the builder proved it with a test instead (stock of the first line restored when the second line throws a ShopFault).
why: The backend docs cover rollback for interceptors and for integration test modes (AUTO_ROLLBACK) but not the runtime rule for custom operations; the builder's kb search for the rule found nothing.
workaround: Integration-style Playwright test proves the rollback of stock, cart and order.

what: Order numbers come from the platform SEQUENCE variable (WS-year-six digits), not from the gap-free document-registry-sequence blueprint; a refused checkout does not use a number, but a number can gap after a rollback or crash.
why: The blueprint needs a lock and a registry entity; the platform sequence is simpler and the builder accepted gaps as documented in platform-behavior-reference.

what: The cart page is a custom component (Cart.tsx) that replaces the generated lines table and shows unit price, line total and total with the shared Price component; values come from the model's derived members (CartLine.lineTotal, CartInfo.total).
why: The generated lines table shows raw numbers (R1-1), and the Price component is the frontend quality bar from FUNCTIONS.md.

what: Add to cart on product cards and details page, via bound custom operation addToCart (Java, customer found by ACTOR email, DAO access); button disabled when out of stock.
why: Level 3 spec: cart belongs to the Customer; add goes on card or details.

what: Adding the same product again increases the quantity of the existing cart line; the operation re-fetches the entity.
why: Level 3 spec: one line with quantity 2.

what: Cart line total (quantity times price), cart total and line count derived in the model; empty cart shows 0.00 EUR; cart page in the Customer menu uses the shared Price component.
why: Level 3 spec: derived numeric with aggregation over a collection.

what: Quantity above stock throws the modeled ShopFault from addToCart; the UI shows a readable snackbar with the stock count and what is already in the cart; nothing is added.
why: Level 3 spec: business fault to readable UI error.

what: Checkout asks for a shipping address (CheckoutInput transfer object), creates the order from the cart, empties the cart and opens the new order via the dialog actions hook; the operation itself is void.
why: Level 3 spec: operation with input transfer object; the output form was blocked by the generator bug.
workaround: See c04-13 and c04-14.

what: Order lines copy product name and unit price at order time (snapshot fields on SalesOrderLine and OrderLineInfo); later price changes do not affect the order line.
why: Level 3 spec: snapshot attributes written by the operation.

what: Checkout decrements stock per line inside the one operation transaction; a test proves the rollback (stock restored, cart kept, no order) when a later line fails with a ShopFault.
why: Level 3 spec: prove the rollback with a test.

what: Order numbers WS-year-six digits from the SalesOrder platform sequence (VariableResolver SEQUENCE); test checks consecutive numbers. Admin gets a read-only Orders list (no create, update or delete).
why: Level 3 spec: order numbers and admin read only orders.
